To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the first deep learning model to detect plaque in optical coherence tomography images.

we present a novel data set of IVOCT images with expert annotations for plaque detection, that we propose and evaluate different deep learning architectures for automatic plaque detection and that we find a multi path model with a polar image representation to perform best.
we propose a novel data set for plaque detection in optical coherence tomography, and we present a new deep learning based method for plaque detection that achieves high accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of plaque deposits in intravascular optical tomography images.
automatic plaque detection for clinical decision support.
the automatic detection of plaque from intravascular optical imaging data using deep learning techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
deep learning based plaque classification is possible and that it outperforms state of the art approaches.
deep learning based approaches are promising candidates for clinical decision support systems in the near future.
the deep learning based approach for automatic plaque detection and differentiation in IVOCT pullbacks is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep learning based approaches can be successfully applied for automatic plaque detection and differentiation from in vivo images.
we have shown how to build a robust and reliable deep learning system that can be used to detect and differentiate plaques in IV-OCT images.
we can achieve a high accuracy of 91,7% with a sensitivity of 91% and a specificity 93%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of transfer learning, polar representation, data augmentation, and multi path architecture can be used as a blueprint for future clinical applications.
deep learning methods are promising for the detection of coronary plaques.
deep learning models are capable of detecting and differentiating between different types of plaque in in vivo images.
